case_title.quote: PARGAN SINGH V. STATE OF PUNJAB & ANR.
case_title.reason: Case title matches the judgment header.

number_of_accused.quote: the two appellant challenge the veracity
number_of_accused.reason: Two appellants are before the Court and both are convicted.

accused_gender.quote: two sikh gentlemen came on scooter
accused_gender.reason: Accused are described as male 'sikh gentlemen'.

accused_age.reason: No age of the accused appears in the judgment.

accused_religion.quote: two sikh gentlemen with trimmed beard
accused_religion.reason: Accused are described by religious identity as Sikh.

accused_caste.reason: No caste or community is named for the accused.

accused_socioeconomic_status.reason: No statement on the accused's wealth or class.

previous_criminal_record.reason: The judgment does not mention any prior criminal record.

victim_gender.quote: fired at victim-deceased and snatched a money bag from him
victim_gender.reason: Victim is referred to with the male pronoun 'him'.

victim_caste.reason: No caste or community is named for the victim.

victim_religion.reason: Victim's religion is not stated; name alone cannot be used.

accused_victim_relationship.quote: the two accused-appellants ... unknown to the complainant or other persons
accused_victim_relationship.reason: Judgment says assailants were unknown to the witnesses, so stranger is supported.

offence_category.quote: Murder of one and grievous injury to another
offence_category.reason: Main offence is murder under s.302 IPC.

statutory_provisions.quote: under sections 302, 307, 397 IPC read with Section 34, IPC
statutory_provisions.reason: Charged sections 302, 307, 397 each read with s.34 match the judgment.

weapon.quote: started firing with pistol on Varun Kumar

evidence_type.quote: PW-2 and PW-3 were eyewitnesses ... PW-1 extra-judicial confession
evidence_type.reason: Eyewitness, medical and extra-judicial confession evidence are all described.

confession.quote: we see no reason to differ with the conclusions ... extra-judicial confession before him
confession.reason: Confession to PW-1 is accepted but treated as weak and needing corroboration; court relied on eyewitnesses.

aggravating_circumstances.correct_value: Assailants shot dead Varun Kumar (the victim), who was companion of PW-2; they then fired at PW-2 who tried to stop them, causing serious injury; cash and cheque book taken
aggravating_circumstances.quote: the assailants who had shot dead Varun Kumar, companion of PW-2. Thereafter, they had fired at PW-2 as well.
aggravating_circumstances.reason: Value wrongly calls the killed person the victim's companion and calls PW-2 a bystander; the victim was killed.

mitigating_circumstances.reason: No mitigating facts are noted by the court.

trial_court_outcome.quote: For the offence under Section 302 IPC ... life and fine of Rs.50,000/- ... 307 IPC ... 10 years ... Rs.25,000/- ... Section 397 IPC ... 10 years
trial_court_outcome.reason: Convictions and sentences under ss.302, 307, 397 with concurrent terms match the judgment.

high_court_outcome.quote: the High Court has dismissed their appeals ... judgment dated 13.12.2012
high_court_outcome.reason: High Court dismissed the appeals, upholding conviction and sentence.

final_outcome.quote: these appeals are bereft of any merit and are accordingly dismissed
final_outcome.reason: Supreme Court dismissed the appeals, so convictions stand.

offence_finally_established.quote: convicted the appellants under Section 302, 397 as well as Section 307 IPC read with Section 34 IPC
offence_finally_established.reason: Convictions under ss.302, 307 and 397, each read with s.34, stand.

imprisonment_type.quote: sentence of rigorous imprisonment of life
imprisonment_type.reason: Final sentence for the main offence under s.302 is life imprisonment.

imprisonment_years.reason: Life sentence is not a fixed term, so null is appropriate.

fine_rs.quote: fine of Rs.50,000/- each ... fine of Rs.25,000/-is imposed
fine_rs.reason: Only the s.302 fine is recorded; the s.307 fine of Rs.25,000 is omitted.

neutral_facts.reason: Summary covers the incident, investigation and evidence without names, outcomes or court references, and does not reveal the decision.

offence_severity.reason: Judgment does not state the statutory prescribed punishment, only sentences imposed.

attempt_completion.quote: the assailants shot dead Varun Kumar
attempt_completion.reason: Main offence of murder was completed by death of victim.

physical_harm.quote: lacerated wound ... upper half of scapula and back bone ... severe haemorrhage and shock
physical_harm.reason: Victim's fatal gunshot wound and companion's multiple injuries are described accurately.

number_of_offences.quote: under sections 302, 307, 397 IPC read with Section 34, IPC
number_of_offences.reason: Three sections charged and all three convictions upheld.

financial_property_loss.quote: withdrew a sum of Rs. 4 lakhs ... snatched the money bag which was also having one cheque book
financial_property_loss.reason: Cash of Rs.4 lakhs and cheque book taken are both described.

premeditation_planning.reason: Court does not find premeditation or planning.

motive.quote: snatched the money bag from him
motive.reason: Robbery of the cash bag is the alleged motive and is marked as alleged.

key_evidence_accepted.correct_value: Eyewitness testimony of PW-2 and PW-3, and extra-judicial confession to PW-1 (corroborated by the eyewitnesses); medical evidence was noted but not expressly relied on by the Supreme Court
key_evidence_accepted.quote: even if for the sake of arguments, we discard the testimony of PW-1, the evidence of two eye-witnesses ... is sufficient
key_evidence_accepted.reason: Supreme Court relied on eyewitnesses; it did not expressly rely on medical evidence.

witness_credibility.quote: The testimony of an injured witness requires a higher degree of credibility
witness_credibility.reason: Matches the court's assessment of PW-2, PW-3 and PW-1.

post_offence_conduct.quote: No reason was given as to why the appellants refused to participate in Test Identification Parade
post_offence_conduct.reason: Refusal of identification parade without reason is noted; no absconding is recorded.

custody_duration.quote: both the accused were apprehended and arrested
custody_duration.reason: Arrest date given; no custody duration is stated.

bail_history.reason: No bail information appears in the judgment.

trial_duration.quote: trial court convicted ... dated 25.09.2008 ... High Court ... 13.12.2012
trial_duration.reason: All listed dates are supported by the judgment.

legal_representation.quote: Mr. Shreepal Singh (who appeared for appellant Pargan Singh) and Shri Shiv Kumar Suri (who argued for the appellant Harminder Singh)
legal_representation.reason: Counsel for accused and State are correctly identified.

investigation_status.quote: FIR was registered ... challan against the appellants was presented before the Court
investigation_status.reason: FIR, seizures, arrest and challan are all supported by the judgment.

procedural_irregularity.reason: Court notes no procedural lapse; the identification-parade argument was rejected as raised late.

appeal_history.quote: High Court has dismissed their appeals ... these appeals are ... dismissed
appeal_history.reason: Outcomes at trial, High Court and Supreme Court are correctly stated.

prosecution_argument.quote: 90 seconds was more than sufficient time for these witnesses to observe the assailants
prosecution_argument.reason: Prosecution arguments on eyewitnesses, injured witness, PW-1 independence and late plea are supported.

defence_argument.quote: the appellants were falsely framed in the said crime
defence_argument.reason: Defence arguments on suspect story, police station showing, and identification after 7 years are supported.

legal_principle_applied.quote: Keeping in view the nature of incident, 90 seconds was too long a period ... eye-witness
legal_principle_applied.reason: Identification depending on circumstances, injured-witness credibility and weak extra-judicial confession are all applied.

precedent_relied_upon.quote: Balwinder Singh v. State of Punjab, (1995) Supp (4) SCC 259
precedent_relied_upon.reason: Balwinder Singh is the only precedent cited and is relied on for extra-judicial confession.

sentencing_rationale.reason: Court did not discuss sentencing reasons; upheld the trial sentence without rationale.

judicial_aggravating_factors.reason: Court did not weigh aggravating factors for sentencing; seriousness was noted only for conviction under s.307.

other_sentence_order.reason: No compensation, directions or other orders are made.
